important.name: A minor divider with fewer than four trailing dashes is neither a divider nor flagged
important.summary:
_MINOR (writing_comments_api.py:18) requires `-{4,}` after the title, and _SEPARATOR_RUN (line 19) needs a run of four separator characters. A short hand-written minor such as `# -- writers --` or `# -- writers ---` matches neither: it is silently treated as prose, drops out of the outline and raises no flag. comment_format.md:48 says a minor line shorter than the width gets a `width` flag, and the CommentsConfig schema description says a minor divider of another length gets a width flag; this short minor gets neither the flag nor a place in the outline.

Also (skill_package): comment_format.md:41-48 says comment_sections.py flags every non-canonical form, including 'a rule or minor line shorter ... than the width' (`width`), and SKILL.md:33-35 makes a flag-free rerun the gate ('never count dashes by eye: the command measures the width'). The recognizer in writing_comments_api.py only treats `# -- <title> -{4,}` as a minor divider (_MINOR, line 18) and only flags a style issue on a run of 4+ separator characters (_SEPARATOR_RUN, line 19). A hand-written `# -- writers ---` or `# -- helpers --` matches neither, so it is classed as prose: no `minor` line, no `width` flag. Verified: sections('# -- writers ---\nx = 1\n# -- helpers --\n', 88) returns dividers=[] flags=[]. That short, eyeballed minor divider is exactly the shape the skill tries to prevent, and the gate lets it through.

Also (runtime): FlagKind.STYLE is documented as 'a separator comment in no canonical form' (writing_comments_models.py:20-21), and comment_format.md:99 bans Unicode dashes. But _SEPARATOR_RUN (writing_comments_api.py:19) matches only ASCII `-=*~_#`, so common legacy separators such as `# ──── Helpers ────` or `# ══════` pass as plain prose with no flag.

Also (overall): _MINOR needs four or more trailing dashes, and _SEPARATOR_RUN needs a run of four, so `# -- helpers --` and `# -- helpers` are neither dividers nor flags (probed at the head: both give dividers=[] flags=[]). These are the most likely malformed minor dividers, and the checker says nothing about them. That works against the skill's 'rerun until no flag' loop.

Also (overall): Any full-line comment with a run of four of `-=*~_#` is a `style` flag (writing_comments_api.py:19,99-100), so an ASCII table border such as `# +------+------+` or a diagram is reported as a non-canonical divider (probed at the head). FlagKind's docstring calls `style` 'a separator comment in no canonical form', and these comments are not separators. Because the skill says to clear every flag in the lines written, a session could end up rewriting a legitimate diagram.

Also (overall): writing_comments_api.py holds several groups of definitions: patterns and types, canonical-line builders, scanning helpers, the _Scan class, and the public sections/report_lines. SKILL.md:21-25 says such a module gets a major divider per group before it is called done, and it has none. A reader who runs comment_sections.py on the convention's reference implementation gets `no dividers`.

Also (system_shape): SKILL.md:21-25 says a module the work creates that holds more than one group of definitions gets a major divider per top-level group 'before it is called done', and 'four definitions in two groups is already two sections' (also comment_format.md:55-57). plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/writing_comments_api.py is new, 125 lines, and holds at least four groups (patterns and the Comments type at 17-22; canonical line builders rule_line/minor_line at 25-33; tokenize reader and banner matcher at 36-60; the _Scan accumulator at 63-100; the public sections/report_lines API at 103-125) with no divider at all. writing_comments_models.py (enums at 12-25, models at 28-54) is the same shape. The first modules written under the convention contradict it, and they are listed in the skill's freeze ledger (docs/plans/freezes/skill/writing-comments/r1.1-freeze.json:11-12).

Also (roast): `other()` flags a comment as `style` when `_SEPARATOR_RUN.search(text)` matches anywhere in it (writing_comments_api.py:19,99). A markdown table row in a comment ('# |------|------|') and a commented string ('# x = "____"') both come back as style flags (probed). The skill sends the session to 'fix every flag', so these false positives become pressure to rewrite comments that are not dividers. The 4-run threshold is the plan's recorded value; anchoring the match keeps that value and stops matching mid-comment.
fix: Relax the trailing run in _MINOR to `-+` (`# -- (?P<title>[^\s-].*?) -+`), so any `# -- <title> -...` line is recognized as a minor divider and check_width flags its length; add a test case for `# -- writers --`.
Alternatively, flag any comment that starts with `# -- ` and fails _MINOR as `style` in _Scan.other.

Loosen the minor pattern to any trailing dash run, e.g. `_MINOR = re.compile(r"# -- (?P<title>[^\s-].*?) -+")`, so a short minor line is recognized and then raises `width` through check_width; add a test in tests/lib/test_writing_comments_api.py for `# -- writers ---` and `# -- helpers --` expecting a minor divider plus a `width` flag.
Alternatively flag `style` for any full-line comment that starts with `# -- ` and does not fullmatch _MINOR, and add the matching row to the table in comment_format.md.
Extend the character class to cover the box-drawing block and Unicode dashes, e.g. `[-=*~_#\u2500-\u257F\u2010-\u2015]{4,}`, and add a test case.

In _Scan.other, flag `style` for a comment that starts with `# -- ` and has a title but does not fullmatch _MINOR (for example `re.fullmatch(r"# -- \S.*", text)`). Add API tests for `# -- helpers --` and `# -- helpers`.

Count only lines where the separator run makes up most of the text after `#` (for example `[-=*~_# ]` covers at least half the text, or the text begins or ends with the run). Add a test that `# +------+------+` raises no flag.
Keep the rule and state in comment_format.md that a `style` flag on a diagram or table border is expected and left alone.

Add major dividers to writing_comments_api.py (for example Patterns, Canonical lines, Scanning, Public API) and check them with comment_sections.py. This changes a part listed in the frozen SkillSpec, so it needs `freeze --refreeze`.

Reopen the writing-comments spec, add canonical major dividers per group to writing_comments_api.py (and writing_comments_models.py), run comment_sections.py on both until it prints no flag, then refreeze.
If library modules in this repository are meant to be exempt, state that scope in SKILL.md's Scope section and comment_format.md 'When a module gets dividers' so the rule and the code agree.

Anchor the separator test to where a divider puts its run, e.g. `re.compile(r"#+\s*[-=*~_#]{4,}")` with `.match(text)`, plus a trailing-run check if wanted. Keep the two existing style tests ('### ======= ... ###' and the dash run before 'scaffold'), which still match, and add a test that a table row stays unflagged.

important.name: A UTF-8 BOM hides line 1 and raises a false banner flag
important.summary:
comment_sections.py reads each file with encoding="utf-8", so a file saved with a byte-order mark (common on Windows) reaches sections() with a leading U+FEFF. _full_line_comments treats the comment on line 1 as not full-line, because tok.line[:col] is "\ufeff" and str.strip() does not remove U+FEFF. A probe at the head shows the effect: a BOM-prefixed source of rule / title / rule reports no divider and a `banner` flag on line 3. SKILL.md tells the session to fix every flag and rerun until none is left, and no edit to the dividers clears this one. The sibling writing_docstrings_api.py already reads with utf-8-sig.

Also (roast): comment_sections.py reads files with encoding="utf-8", which keeps a leading U+FEFF. In `_full_line_comments` (writing_comments_api.py:41) the line-1 comment then fails the `not tok.line[:col].strip()` test, because str.strip() does not treat U+FEFF as whitespace. A canonical banner on line 1 is dropped. Probed on the project interpreter: '\ufeff' + rule/'# T'/rule returns dividers=[] and a `banner` flag on the closing rule at line 3. The skill tells the session to 'rerun until none is left', but no edit to the banner clears this flag, so on Windows, where editors still write BOMs, the loop never ends.

Also (runtime): comment_sections.py:69 reads with encoding="utf-8", which keeps a leading U+FEFF. In _full_line_comments (writing_comments_api.py:41), `tok.line[:col].strip()` does not strip U+FEFF, so a full-line comment on line 1 of a BOM-prefixed file is not counted. When it is counted, its column is off by one for the width check.
fix: Read with `path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")` at comment_sections.py:69, and add a command test with a BOM-prefixed banner file that expects `major` on line 1 and no flag.
Strip one leading "\ufeff" in `writing_comments_api.sections` before tokenizing, so API callers get the same result, and add an API test for it.
Read the file with encoding="utf-8-sig" in comment_sections.py:69 and add a command test with a BOM-prefixed banner on line 1.
Strip a leading "\ufeff" from `source` at the top of `sections()` (writing_comments_api.py:106), so API callers are covered too, and pin it with an API test.
Read with encoding="utf-8-sig" in comment_sections.py:69 (decode errors still surface as ValueError).

important.name: comment_sections.py prints comment text without a UTF-8 stdout, so a non-ASCII comment crashes the command on Windows
important.summary: main() prints divider titles and flag texts verbatim (comment_sections.py:83), outside the try block, with stdout left at the locale encoding. hpy does not set PYTHONUTF8 or PYTHONIOENCODING, so on Windows a piped stdout is cp1252. A module holding a legacy separator such as `#### ═══ AREA ═══ ####` (flagged `style`, text echoed) or a title with an arrow raises UnicodeEncodeError: a traceback, no `problem:` line, and output lost. That breaks the docstring contract (every failure is one `problem:` line, exit 1), and the non-canonical Unicode separators the convention bans are exactly the comments this command exists to report. Sibling commands (plan.py:1172, parallel2.py:700, bubble_memo.py:555, review_models.py:661) already reconfigure stdout for this reason.
fix: At the top of main(), add `if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"): sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")` (and the same for sys.stderr, since problem lines echo file names), matching plan.py:1172; add a test in tests/skills/test_comment_sections_command.py whose fixture holds a non-cp1252 comment.
Print through the existing UTF-8-safe helper in harness_lib/review_models.py:661 (or a shared copy of it) instead of a bare print.

minor.name: divider_width minimum 1 admits widths no canonical divider can fill
minor.summary:
The schema accepts any integer >= 1 for comments.divider_width, and config.py:562 mirrors that. rule_line (writing_comments_api.py:25-27) and minor_line (writing_comments_api.py:30-33) pad with max(4, ...) dashes, so a rule is never shorter than indent + 2 + 4 = 6 characters. With a width below 6, every canonical divider the command writes fails check_width (writing_comments_api.py:75-78) and gets a width flag, so no source can pass. The description promises 'a rule or minor divider of another length gets a width flag', which a width of 1 to 5 can never satisfy.

Also (overall): The schema and _comments accept any divider_width >= 1, but a rule needs `# ` plus at least four dashes (6 characters; _RULE and rule_line's max(4, ...)), and a minor line needs `# -- t ` plus four dashes (11 or more). With a width below 6, every rule gets a `width` flag that no edit can clear.
fix: Raise the schema minimum to a value the generators can fill (6 at column 0; a larger floor if indented dividers must fit) and mirror it in _comments in config.py.
Leave the minimum at 1 and add a sentence to the description that widths below the generators' 4-dash floor flag every divider.
Raise the floor to 6 in harness.schema.json (`minimum: 6`) and in _comments (`width < 6`), add the value 5 to the bad cases in both test_config.py tests, and note the floor in the README key row.

minor.name: Quick reference row conflicts with the Scope rules for a touched module
minor.summary: SKILL.md:41 says a non-canonical divider is rewritten when the work rewrites the block it heads. SKILL.md:43 says that for a module the work does not change, the skill should offer a section pass in the reply. The quick reference row at line 52 ("Editing one function in a module with odd dividers | Leave the dividers; mention them if asked") conflicts with both. It drops the rewrite case for the block the work rewrites. It also gives a module the work changes less reporting than an unchanged one: mention only if asked, versus an unprompted offer.
fix: Change the line 52 call to "Leave dividers outside the rewritten block; rewrite the one heading a block the work rewrites; offer a section pass in the reply" so it matches lines 41 and 43, then refreeze the spec.
Or change line 43 so it applies to both cases, and have the quick-reference row point to it.

minor.name: Docstring says every path is relative to the project; _label falls back to absolute
minor.summary:
comment_sections.py:10 states 'Each path is relative to the project.' _label (lines 53-57) returns the absolute POSIX path when a file sits outside the resolved root. That happens whenever --repo names another project, or when later files live in a different repository from the first.

Also (skill_package): comment_sections.py:10 says 'Each path is relative to the project.' _label (lines 53-57) returns path.as_posix(), an absolute path, when a file sits outside the resolved root. That happens with `--repo` pointing at another project, or with files from two repositories where the root comes from the first one. The fallback is reasonable, but the docstring overstates it.

Also (overall): comment_sections.py:10 says 'Each path is relative to the project', but _label (lines 53-57) prints the absolute posix path for a file outside the project root, for example a file named alongside `--repo` that points at another project.

Also (system_shape): comment_sections.py:10 says 'Each path is relative to the project.' _label (53-57) returns path.as_posix(), an absolute path, for a file outside the resolved project root: a second file from another repository, or a --repo that does not hold the file. The docstring states the common case as a guarantee.
fix: Reword the docstring: 'Each path is relative to the project, or absolute for a file outside it.'
Change comment_sections.py:10 to 'Each path is relative to the project, or absolute when the file lies outside it.'
Reword line 10 to 'Each path is relative to the project, or absolute when the file sits outside it.'
Change line 10 to 'Each path is relative to the project, or absolute for a file outside it.'

minor.name: Format file says every problem line names a path
minor.summary:
comment_format.md:115 says "A `problem:` line names a path to fix." comment_sections.py also prints a problem line that names no path: when no file is given (`no file named; pass one or more .py files`, `_resolve`), and when the configuration is invalid (`ConfigError` caught in `main`). An agent following the reference would look for a path in those lines and find none.

Also (system_shape): comment_format.md:109-113 shows line 77 as only 'src/mod.py:77: flag width: # -- writers ---...' (a 73-character minor divider). The API keeps an off-width minor divider and flags it (writing_comments_api.py:96-98; pinned by test_a_divider_short_of_the_width_is_kept_and_flagged), and report_lines prints the divider row before the flag row on the same line (writing_comments_api.py:119-125). The real output is 'src/mod.py:77: minor writers' followed by the flag line, so a session matching the documented shape sees an unexpected extra line.
fix: Reword line 115 to "A `problem:` line on stderr (exit 1, nothing on stdout) names what to fix: a missing or non-`.py` path, source that does not tokenize, no path given, or an invalid configuration." Then refreeze the spec.
Insert 'src/mod.py:77: minor writers' above the flag line in the example block at comment_format.md:110-112.

minor.name: Non-object comments value is not in the no-jsonschema cases
minor.summary: _comments (config.py:556-557) raises `comments: must be an object` when the section is not a dict; deep_merge (config.py:318-319) replaces the default dict with a scalar, so that branch is reachable from a project file. test_invalid_comments_raise_without_jsonschema covers only dict-shaped bad values, so the fallback type check for the section itself is unguarded.
fix: Add a case `"x"` (or `[]`) to the parametrize list at tests/lib/test_config.py:44-51 and widen the `bad` annotation to `Any`, or add a one-off test asserting `ConfigError` matching `^comments: must be an object` with jsonschema masked.

minor.name: Banner-rejection branches, opening-rule width and indented flag text are untested
minor.summary: _banner_end (writing_comments_api.py:48-60) rejects a banner on a title at another indentation, a title that is itself a rule, and an empty `#` title; the tests cover only a missing closing rule (line 32) and a missing title (line 73). The width check on the opening rule (writing_comments_api.py:88) is covered only on the closing rule (line 51), and CommentFlag's 'indentation removed' text contract (writing_comments_models.py:39) has no indented flagged line. Each branch could be deleted without a test failing.

minor.name: report_lines same-line tie-break is untested
minor.summary: report_lines' docstring (writing_comments_api.py:119-120) promises a divider before a flag on its own line, implemented by the 0/1 sort key at writing_comments_api.py:121-122. test_report_lines_list_dividers_and_flags_in_line_order puts the divider and the flag on different lines (1, 4, 5), so swapping or dropping the tie-break key passes the suite.
fix: Add a test: `short = "# -- row helpers " + "-" * 69`; assert `report_lines("src/mod.py", sections(f"{short}\n", 88)) == ["src/mod.py:1: minor row helpers", f"src/mod.py:1: flag width: {short}"]`.

minor.name: comment_sections.py --repo and two documented problem paths are untested
minor.summary:
The command docstring (comment_sections.py:10-14) promises that the project is `--repo` when given, else the first file's project, and that an invalid configuration and a file that does not decode as UTF-8 are each one `problem:` line with exit 1. No test in tests/skills/test_comment_sections_command.py passes `--repo`, writes an invalid `comments` block, or writes non-UTF-8 bytes; every test runs with cwd at the project and the files inside it. A regression in the `--repo` branch at comment_sections.py:63 (for example resolving against the first file instead of `--repo`) or in the `ConfigError`/`UnicodeDecodeError` catch would pass the suite.

Also (tests): The command contract is one `problem:` line on stderr. test_a_missing_file_is_a_problem_line_and_prints_nothing (line 76) and test_no_path_is_a_problem_line (line 101) assert `stderr.startswith("problem: ")`, but test_a_non_python_file_is_a_problem_line (80-85) and test_unparsable_source_is_a_problem_line (88-93) only check that the path appears in stderr, so a traceback naming the path would also pass them despite their names.
fix: Add three subprocess tests: (1) two make_project repos, one with `{"comments": {"divider_width": 60}}`, run from the other with `--repo <narrow root>` on a 60-wide banner file in the narrow root and assert the single `major` line and no width flag; (2) `make_project({"comments": {"divider_width": 0}}, files={"src/a.py": "x = 1\n"})` asserts exit 1, empty stdout, stderr starting `problem: `; (3) write `b"# \xff\n"` to `src/bin.py` with `write_bytes`, assert exit 1, empty stdout and `src/bin.py` in stderr.
Add `assert done.stderr.startswith("problem: ")` to both tests, at lines 85 and 93.
